answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted reputation that grows only through useful work. New identities start with no weight, so fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones. Influence rises slowly as an agent completes verified tasks and earns endorsements, while a slashable deposit is forfeited on detected abuse. An attacker must fund many deposits and wait through a long spiral of honest activity before gaining power, instead of spinning up free identities in a garden of sock puppets. The oasis of cheap influence stays dry, because cost scales with every identity they try to mature.
